title: 2026年6月四级真题 第3套 阅读1
paperTitle: 2026年6月大学英语四级真题（第3套）
passage:
P1 Disgust is a universal human emotion. One type of disgust is called physical disgust, which protects us from eating or touching things that could be dangerous for us, such as raw meat or insects. Children experience physical disgust from a very early age, but do not achieve an understanding of the concept until they are around four years old.

P2 Some researchers maintain that there is another type of disgust, called moral disgust, that protects us from engaging in activities that can be perceived as morally wrong. Examples of moral disgust are stealing, lying or cheating.

P3 However, not all academics think that moral disgust really exists. Some say that when we refer to disgust in relation to moral issues, we are using disgust as a metaphor(隐喻), and what we are feeling is in reality anger.

P4 If moral disgust appears quite late in development, it makes sense to think that there is actually a social component to it. Children learn about emotions in many different ways. Of special relevance are parents-children conversations about emotions. Indeed, children whose parents talk about emotions often have a better emotional understanding than children whose parents do not discuss emotions often.

P5 However, there are no studies that have examined how parents and children talk about disgust. This is what we set up to examine in our study.

P6 We asked 68 English-speaking mothers and their four-, six- or eight-year-old children to discuss some stories about moral and physical disgust. Our preliminary findings show mothers and children do talk about disgust, but mainly about physical disgust and not so much about moral disgust.

P7 When we asked mothers and children to discuss moral issues, such as whether it is OK to play with a child who has stolen someone else's snack, they linked this type of moral wrongdoing with the emotion of anger and not disgust.

P8 Does this mean that moral disgust does not exist? Some researchers suggest moral disgust exists in adults. Our findings suggest that moral disgust is either understood at a later age or is only used metaphorically, if at all, in children as old as eight years.

questions.q: What does the passage tell us about physical disgust?
options: It is an emotion as contrasted with thoughts.
It is a concept beyond children's understanding.
It is a mechanism to keep us from being harmed.
It is an experience gained from any form of danger.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the passage tell us about physical disgust?是在问文章对physical disgust的 客观说明，不涉及推理、态度或主旨。

【拆句】What does the passage tell us about physical disgust?是主谓宾结构的特殊疑问句，主 语the passage，谓语tell，间接宾语us，直接宾语由what充当，about physical disgust限 定话题范围，无否定、比较等陷阱。

【定位】One type of disgust is called physical disgust, which protects us from eating or touching things that could be dangerous for us, such as raw meat or insects. 厌恶感的一种类型被称为生理厌恶，它保护我们不去吃或触碰可能对我们有危险的东西，比 如生肉或昆虫。

【选项】A) 偷换概念 It is an emotion as contrasted with thoughts.在原文Disgust is a universal human emotion.基础上添加了未出现的"as contrasted with thoughts"，把客观陈述偷换成对 立关系。 B) 与原文相反 It is a concept beyond children's understanding.截取了do not achieve an understanding of the concept until they are around four years old中的否定，却忽 略"until around four"，将"暂时未理解"反转为"永远无法理解"。 C) ✓ 正确 physical disgust, which protects us from eating or touching things that could be dangerous for us ↔It is a mechanism to keep us from being harmed. It is a mechanism to keep us from being harmed.与protects us from eating or touching things that could be dangerous for us形成语法层面的同义改写，是最佳 选项。 D) 偷换概念 It is an experience gained from any form of danger.将定位句中的"protects us from eating or touching things that could be dangerous"改为"experience gained from danger"，把防御机制篡改为经验来源，且any form of danger绝对化。 一些研究人员如何看待道德厌恶？ A) 它往往会出现在各种形式的不当行为中。 B) 它和身体厌恶一样令人厌烦。 C) 这是普通人用来描述愤怒的一个术语。 D) 它阻止人们做任何道德上错误的事情。

questions.q: How do some researchers perceive moral disgust?
options: It tends to appear in various forms of wrongdoing.
It is just as annoying to people as physical disgust.
It is a term used by common folk to describe anger.
It stops people from doing anything morally wrong.
questions.explain:
【判型】How do some researchers perceive moral disgust?是在问some researchers对moral disgust的具体看法，属于文中可直接找到的事实。

【拆句】How do some researchers perceive moral disgust?是特殊疑问句，主语some researchers，谓语perceive，宾语moral disgust；how询问方式/看法，整体结构平直。

【定位】Some researchers maintain that there is another type of disgust, called moral disgust, that protects us from engaging in activities that can be perceived as morally wrong. 一些研究者认为还存在另一种厌恶，称为道德厌恶，它保护我们不去做那些可能被视为道德 错误的行为。

【选项】A) 以偏概全 It tends to appear in various forms of wrongdoing.把Examples of moral disgust are stealing, lying or cheating.中的举例包装成"moral disgust本身以多种形式出现"， 混淆了"触发它的行为"与"它本身"。 B) 无中生有 It is just as annoying to people as physical disgust.使用just as...as结构，但原文从 未比较两种厌恶的annoying程度，也未评价其是否annoying。 C) 张冠李戴 It is a term used by common folk to describe anger.源于Some say that when we refer to disgust in relation to moral issues, we are using disgust as a metaphor(隐 喻), and what we are feeling is in reality anger.，但该观点是some academics而非 some researchers，且common folk缩小了原句we的范围。 D) ✓ 正确 protects us from engaging in activities that can be perceived as morally wrong ↔ It stops people from doing anything morally wrong. It stops people from doing anything morally wrong.与protects us from engaging in activities that can be perceived as morally wrong.在语义场和语法结构上均对应， 是正确项。 为什么道德厌恶在儿童的发展过程中出现得相当晚？ A) 它需要通过社会互动来学习。 B) 他们对其学习过程几乎没有控制力。 C) 它对他们来说过于复杂，难以掌握。 D) 他们的父母很少谈论情绪。

questions.q: Why does moral disgust appear quite late in children's development?
options: It needs to be learnt through social interactions.
They have little control over its learning process.
It is too complex for them to acquire.
Their parents seldom talk about emotions.
questions.explain:
【判型】Why does moral disgust appear quite late in children's development?不是直接引用某 个事实句，而是要求从文中因果解释中推进一步。

【拆句】Why does moral disgust appear quite late in children's development?是why引导的特 殊疑问句，主语moral disgust，谓语appear，状语quite late in children's development；询问原因，需在定位句附近找因果解释。

【定位】If moral disgust appears quite late in development, it makes sense to think that there is actually a social component to it. Children learn about emotions in many different ways. 如果道德厌恶在成长过程中出现得相当晚，那么认为它实际上具有社会成分是合理的。儿童 以多种方式学习情绪。

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 social component to it. Children learn about emotions in many different ways ↔ It needs to be learnt through social interactions. It needs to be learnt through social interactions.是原文因果链的一步推理，既未跳 跃也未添加新信息。 B) 无中生有 They have little control over its learning process.引入control概念，但原文Children learn about emotions in many different ways只说学习方式多，未涉及控制程度。 C) 过度推断 It is too complex for them to acquire.用too...to结构把原文的"late"和"social component"臆断为复杂度问题，原文未出现complex或acquire difficulty。 D) 与原文相反 Their parents seldom talk about emotions.与children whose parents talk about emotions often have a better emotional understanding than children whose parents do not discuss emotions often.直接相反，原文强调父母经常谈情绪。 作者和他的同事想在实验中考察什么？ A) 父母会告诉孩子哪些反对道德不当行为的话。 B) 父母和孩子会把道德不当行为与什么联系起来。 C) 4岁、6岁和8岁的儿童如何看待道德厌恶。 D) 父母和孩子之间如何谈论厌恶。

questions.q: What did the author and his colleagues want to examine in their experiment?
options: What parents tell children against moral wrongdoing.
What parents and children link moral wrongdoing to.
How moral disgust is seen by children aged 4, 6 and 8.
How disgust is discussed between parents and children.
questions.explain:
【判型】What did the author and his colleagues want to examine in their experiment?直接询 问研究目的，文中有明确对应句。 49. What did the author and his colleagues want to examine in their experiment? A) What parents tell children against moral wrongdoing. B) What parents and children link moral wrongdoing to. C) How moral disgust is seen by children aged 4, 6 and 8. D) How disgust is discussed between parents and children.

【拆句】What did the author and his colleagues want to examine in their experiment?是what 引导的特殊疑问句，主语the author and his colleagues，谓语want to examine，in their experiment限定范围；did提示过去时，对应文中已完成的研究。

【定位】However, there are no studies that have examined how parents and children talk about disgust. This is what we set up to examine in our study. 然而，还没有研究考察过父母和孩子如何谈论厌恶。这正是我们研究要考察的问题。

【选项】A) 偷换概念 What parents tell children against moral wrongdoing.把how parents and children talk about disgust中的talk about disgust替换为tell children against moral wrongdoing，范围收窄且改变了话题。 B) 答非所问 What parents and children link moral wrongdoing to.对应的是they linked this type of moral wrongdoing with the emotion of anger and not disgust.，这是实验 结果，不是作者想考察的问题。 C) 偷换概念 How moral disgust is seen by children aged 4, 6 and 8.把four-, six- or eight-year- old children中的年龄信息放大为研究核心，但原文研究的是父母与孩子如何谈 disgust，而非儿童如何看待moral disgust。 D) ✓ 正确 how parents and children talk about disgust ↔ How disgust is discussed between parents and children. How disgust is discussed between parents and children.与how parents and children talk about disgust. This is what we set up to examine in our study.逐成分 对应，完全等值。 从作者和他的同事的研究结果中，我们可以推断出关于道德厌恶的什么信息？ A) 这是一个儿童几乎无法理解的概念。 B) 八岁以下的儿童很少有道德厌恶。 C) 这是大多数父母与孩子交谈时使用的一个术语。 D) 它存在于具有强烈正义感的成年人身上。

questions.q: What can we infer about moral disgust from the author and his colleagues' findings?
options: It is a notion hardly comprehensible to children.
It rarely exists in children younger than eight.
It is a term most parents use when talking to children.
It exists in adults with a strong sense of justice.
questions.explain:
【判型】What can we infer about moral disgust from the author and his colleagues' findings?要求从研究发现中概括出隐含结论。 50. What can we infer about moral disgust from the author and his colleagues' findings? A) It is a notion hardly comprehensible to children. B) It rarely exists in children younger than eight. C) It is a term most parents use when talking to children. D) It exists in adults with a strong sense of justice.

【拆句】What can we infer about moral disgust from the author and his colleagues' findings?是what引导的特殊疑问句，can infer表示推断，about moral disgust限定对 象，from the author and his colleagues' findings限定推理依据；需要在结论句基础上做 一步概括。

【定位】Our findings suggest that moral disgust is either understood at a later age or is only used metaphorically, if at all, in children as old as eight years. 我们的发现表明，道德厌恶要么在更晚的年龄才能被理解，要么即便存在，在八岁儿童中也 只被隐喻式地使用。

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 either understood at a later age or is only used metaphorically, if at all, in children as old as eight years ↔It is a notion hardly comprehensible to children. It is a notion hardly comprehensible to children.是结论句的一步同义转述，未过度 延伸。 B) 偷换概念 It rarely exists in children younger than eight.把only used metaphorically, if at all 中的使用方式篡改为存在频率，且younger than eight与原文as old as eight不一致。 C) 与原文相反 It is a term most parents use when talking to children.与do talk about disgust, but mainly about physical disgust and not so much about moral disgust.直接相 反，父母并不常使用moral disgust一词。 D) 无中生有 It exists in adults with a strong sense of justice.虽然提到Some researchers suggest moral disgust exists in adults.，但"with a strong sense of justice"是原文 没有的信息。
